summary: El Salvador waives visas for a broad list including the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas; many visitors pay USD 12 for a tourist card when arriving by air or sea. The UK Foreign Office says visitors can travel between El Salvador, Guatemala and Nicaragua for up to 90 days without a visa under the CA-4 agreement. Remaining nationalities need a consular visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Passports in category B of Migración's visa classification (consular visa without consultation) are treated as visa-exempt when the holder has a valid visa from the United States, Canada or the Schengen area; they pay the USD 12 tourist card when arriving by air or sea. Category C passports ("consulted" visa) still need a consular visa even with such a visa.

payments.text: The US dollar is the official currency. The Government of Canada says Canadian credit and debit cards are generally accepted, but $50 and $100 bills are not widely accepted. Australia's Smartraveller says credit cards aren't widely accepted outside major centres and ATMs aren't reliable, and the UK FCDO advises bringing smaller denominations.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says security has improved considerably with significant reductions in crime, but the risks of violent and petty crime still exist. A state of exception in force since 2022 gives police additional powers, and the police may detain you if they suspect you are a gang member, so always carry identification. Canada says officers at checkpoints may consider tattoos an indication of gang membership.

idp.text: El Salvador is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says you can travel between El Salvador, Guatemala and Nicaragua for up to 90 days without a visa under the CA-4 agreement. Migración handles extensions of a tourist stay of up to 90 days (form F44).
The USD 12 tourist card is charged when you arrive by air or sea; the law does not charge it at land borders.

The UK FCDO says a state of exception has been in force since 2022, giving police additional powers that have led to many arrests, sometimes without much evidence. Canada says you may face identity checks: always carry valid identification.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for El Salvador?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not: the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas are visa-exempt for 90 days. Many of these nationalities pay USD 12 for a tourist card on arrival. Nationalities outside the exemption list need a consular visa, or, if their passport is in category B and they hold a valid US, Canadian or Schengen visa, can enter with the tourist card instead.

faq.question: What is the USD 12 tourist card?
faq.answer: An entry fee of USD 12 that the law requires of foreign visitors arriving by air or sea. Visa-exempt nationalities such as US and Canadian passport holders pay it, while Central American neighbours, official-passport holders and nationalities exempt by treaty or reciprocity do not. It is not required at land borders.

faq.question: Does time in Guatemala or Honduras count against my El Salvador stay?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says you can travel between El Salvador, Guatemala and Nicaragua for up to 90 days without a visa under the CA-4 agreement, which also includes Honduras. Migración handles extensions of a tourist stay of up to 90 days (form F44).

faq.question: Is El Salvador safe to visit now?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says security has improved considerably with significant reductions in crime, but the risks of violent and petty crime still exist. A state of exception in force since 2022 gives police additional powers; the UK advises carrying a copy of your passport's photo page, and Canada advises always cooperating with military and police officers and carrying valid identification.
